comment: 1. The heart button is gone from playlists and albums. 2. I still can't add the same song twice to a playlist. 3. Now they're charging more on top of the price hike. I'd pay a small add-on to get the heart back, but this is just nickel and dime stuff.

Honestly a few bucks more is fine for the catalog, but I'd only be happy if the extra actually reaches artists. Right now artists get almost nothing per stream, so I'm not holding my breath. Still paying.

Paying more for Spotify and still no lossless, meanwhile I already pay Tidal for hi-fi. Spotify Connect and Discover Weekly are why it stays in my life, but the price bump without HiFi is a tough sell.
Still worth every penny. I use it every single day, no ads, unlimited skips, offline stuff. A dollar more a month doesn't change that for me at all.

I already cancelled and it still pops up a renewal screen every time I open the app. Now they're raising prices and I'm not even paying. The pop up gets in the way when I just need to pause or skip, very frustrating.
Worth it to me for the features I actually use, and I'll put in the setup effort. Bummed they keep removing stuff without notice though. A price bump doesn't bother me much if the good stuff stays.

Premium is still bang for your buck for me, I use it every day. But ads keep getting heavier and they keep pulling perks without changing the price. Now they raise it too, so I'm watching this closely.
Family plan is still pretty cheap per person and we split it, so it's worth it. The one thing I'd like is clear info on how much our bill changes, since nobody in my house wants surprise charges.

Cool, more money for ad-free music, and I still get podcast ads anyway. The podcast stuff keeps getting shoved down my throat on the home screen. Gotta make money somehow I guess, but Overcast is looking better every week.

Student plan going to 5.99 with Hulu still included is still a steal, honestly. I'd be annoyed if they took Hulu out too, but for now I'm not going anywhere. Downloads for my commute are the main reason I stay.

Premium is still the best value I pay for, more than all my other streaming subs combined. The free tier is useless for what I do. Still wish they would stop shoving pop up suggestions in my face though.

320 kbps is still good enough for AirPods and the car, so the price bump doesn't change much for me. I still don't hear enough difference to pay for lossless, but I'd like to have the option. Not switching over this.

UI changes keep burying my library and they just keep adding AI DJ nonsense. Now the price goes up too. YouTube Music is a great deal with a strong app, I keep looking at it. Still here for the recommendations, but barely.

Price is fine, I've been here a decade. But this home screen with huge blocks of suggestions looks like TikTok and it's absolute garbage. Revert it or I'm cancelling my membership and going to stoop to Tidal or Apple Music.

Price doesn't bother me, I'm mostly here for radio and Discover Weekly, and Spotify is still the most feature-rich thing I've tried. Annoying they removed album radio though. Still a good tool for quick playlists with friends.

Still a fair price for the library, and Discover Weekly still finds me new stuff. Recommendations keep repeating songs I already know though, and the new UI hides Release Radar. Not a dealbreaker for me, still better than Apple Music's algorithm.

Another update, another broken download. I rolled back, cleared cache, reinstalled, and the liked songs list still scrolls like molasses. Support had no fix. Hard to justify paying more when the app keeps breaking.
Rolled back to my old version and turned off auto updates. If they force the new layout on me I'm cancelling the day it lands. Price is not the issue, I just want to listen to music and have it work.

Premium is still worth it for me, shared playlists with friends and Connect are the whole reason I stay. Tidal does better audio for about the same price, but I'm not rebuilding all my playlists. Student plan made this easier at least.
A month of Premium costs less than an hour of my pay, so I'm not mad about it. I can't imagine going back to ads. The renewal prompts after cancelling are the annoying part, but I'm not leaving.

I cancelled over the music tab redesign already. Still the same awful card layout, I want my album tiles back. Price doesn't matter to me, I'm switching to Apple Music, and I'd come back if they turn the old view back.
Hearts are gone from album and track lists, so I can't see which songs I already liked. I'd already unsubscribed once and I'll do it again if they don't come back. Apple Music is sitting right there.
Price doesn't matter to me since I don't pay. Free is still fine for playlists and background music, even with ads every few songs. I'm not sure Premium is worth it for me yet.

Still no true random shuffle, it keeps replaying the same one-hit wonders. On CarPlay a big playlist only plays the liked songs. I love the service overall but this is getting old, and Pandora is looking better.

Price is fine, the real problem is the enhance feature mixing recommended songs into my own playlists. I already cancelled Premium once over this stuff and I use Skiley and stats.fm to work around it. Still here, but barely.

Spotify pays artists fractions of a cent per stream while making huge money, so a price hike with nothing for artists makes me sick. I already moved to Apple Music over royalties and I don't miss the greed. Pay artists more, then we can talk.

Price is not the thing for me. I switched back to Spotify because of Connect and Android Auto, even though Apple Music sounds better. The UI keeps getting cluttered and the podcast push is annoying, so I'm watching the next update.

Premium is still worth it for ad-free music and skipping ads on podcasts in the car, but this home screen is crowded with podcasts and navigation is a mess. I already cancelled a family plan over the interface and I'm looking at Deezer. Price doesn't matter if the app is unusable.
